sample_unit: final agent answers (10,800 simulated plus 1,440 from live open-source harnesses)

links.outcome: Rate of agents disclosing forbidden composite conclusions assembled from accessible documents under benign queries
links.effect: Best model GPT-5.6-Sol disclosed forbidden composites in 7.08% of answers (95% CI 3.75-10.67%) in simulation, with worse rates in live harnesses.
links.quote: Even under benign queries designed to be answerable from one document, GPT-5.6-Sol, the best performing model tested, discloses forbidden composites in 7.08% of answers (95% CI: 3.75-10.67%) in simulation, with worse disclosure rates in live harnesses.

links.outcome: Agent aggregation of accessible documents into unauthorized sensitive disclosures despite safeguards
links.effect: With classification headers and explicit aggregation rules, unsafe disclosures persisted in 32.37% of simulated answers (95% CI 28.33-36.19%) across all intents.
links.quote: Adding visible classification headers and explicit aggregation rules reduces pooled disclosure rates substantially, yet unsafe disclosures persist in 32.37% of simulated answers (95% CI: 28.33-36.19%) across all intents despite these safeguards.

unlisted_practices: Visible classification headers and explicit aggregation rules in agent prompts to prevent mosaic-style confidentiality leaks
Controls on what agents may infer and disclose to mixed-clearance users

screen.practice: visible classification headers and explicit aggregation rules
screen.reason: Evaluates confidential data leakage (mosaic effect) across domains including medical data and tests safeguards like classification headers and aggregation rules.
